final_synthesis: Sleep deprivation significantly impairs cognitive functions such as attention, vigilance, working memory, and decision-making [S1][S2]. Being awake for 17 to 19 hours can lead to performance declines comparable to having a blood alcohol concentration of 0.05% [S1]. Chronic sleep restriction, like getting only six hours per night over two weeks, causes cognitive deficits similar to those from total sleep deprivation but individuals often underestimate their level of impairment [S3]. This underestimation suggests that people may not fully recognize the extent of their cognitive decline due to insufficient sleep.
